plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: Goblet-shaped lilac-pink flowers push straight out of bare soil with no leaves at all. They look like a crocus that has arrived on the wrong date. The strappy foliage comes up in spring and dies back, so autumn gardens get a surprise burst of colour.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late September to October, with flowers open in early October
plants.location: Temperate Europe and gardens across the Pacific Northwest of North America
plants.funFact: Autumn crocus is the source of colchicine, a compound used in medicine and in plant breeding. It is also highly toxic, and the plant is often called 'naked ladies' because the flowers appear without leaves.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Whole streets turn hazy violet-blue as the trees burst into bloom. Clusters of trumpet-shaped flowers carpet the pavements below. The ferny canopy glows in the spring sun of the southern hemisphere.
plants.bloomingSeason: October, in the southern hemisphere spring
plants.location: Pretoria (Jakarandastad), South Africa, and other southern hemisphere cities
plants.funFact: Native to South America, jacarandas were planted in Pretoria in such numbers that the city is nicknamed 'Jacaranda City'. Their October bloom is a local landmark.

plants.name: Nerine bowdenii
plants.description: Frilly, ribbon-petalled pink flowers sparkle on bare stems, as if dusted with frost. They open as the garden fades for the year. Their late show keeps pollinators fed well into autumn.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn, with flowers open through October
plants.location: Gardens in the UK and temperate Europe (native to South Africa)
plants.funFact: Nerine bowdenii comes from the mountains of South Africa's eastern region. Its petals have a glittering sheen, which is why the genus is nicknamed the 'jewel lily'.
